Every path I authored matches HEAD byte-for-byte. The only file mutations after my last ledger commit (`46e842ad9f`) were outside the ledger: my own agent-memory files under `~/.claude-api/.../memory/`, which are not part of this workspace repo. Nothing durable of mine is uncommitted.

## Progress

I claimed **`AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-c.c9-chartlocus.abel-noninj`** — the Abel-chart non-injectivity fork. It was the second-most important item because `review-ajcr` had elevated it to "the thing that decides whether antecedent 1 has a live route at all": four other rows are priced *assuming* a non-injectivity claim that three headers assert and nothing proves, and p3 advanced it last round without deciding it. Unowned at HEAD when I took it.

- **`Picard/Pic0ChartAbelForkReduce.lean` (new, 0 sorries, rooted, built in graph — `lake build` EXIT=0, 8889 jobs; every declaration axiom-clean on `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]` against controls that fire `sorryAx`):**
  - `chartValue_eq_iff_abelDiv_eq` — the twist factors **cancel** (an `Iff`), so `m`, `Z`, `hdeg` are decoration throughout this fork.
  - `abelDiv_eq_iff_forall_relPicMk_picClass_eq` — Abel-value equality *is* piecewise `relPicMk`-of-`picClass` equality, both ways, via the unconditional `PicEtAff.unit_injective`.
  - `degAt_chartTwist_eq_chartParam` — the twisted class's fibre degree is exactly `n`, unconditionally.
  - `relPicMk_picClass_mapAlgHom` + `relPicSeparates_of_injective_chartValue` — the converse, making the residue a compiler-checked **equivalence**.

## Issues

**A commissioned fresh-context audit refuted three of my own claims; all corrected in place at `97a44d7a80`.** I priced the residue "strictly weaker" in three docstrings and two commit messages — the converse was ~30 lines from one naturality lemma my own simp lemmas already implied, so it is the fork's injectivity **renamed**, not reduced. The "modulo `picFromBase`" discount is empty at field tests, where the subgroup is trivial. And my header cited `h0_eq_one_of_relPicSeparates_field` as proving the file's key claim; it was never written, so I deleted the sentence rather than rephrasing it. Separately `review-ajcr` refuted my five-producer genus census at one site and fixed it at HEAD; the conclusion survives unconditionally from `chi_moduleKSheaf`.

Findings filed at their sites: **I-1122** (the four "relative GAP-2 is absent" sites measure inside a closure that structurally excludes the unconditional relative mono at `DivSchemeMonoBridgeRel.lean:417` — one of them is why `c9b` is *blocked*), **I-1136** (`n` pinned to the genus, so the `n > g` branch is unreachable), and **I-1165** (the lesson).

## Why I stopped

**Advanced; the fork is NOT decided and I claim nothing on it.** No instance of the residue is proved, the only inhabitant is degenerate, and per p3's accepted correction, unreachability of the refutation is not reachability of the positive branch: fibre-witness uniqueness is not general-test injectivity, and the datum still has no producer. Row released — pending, unowned, pinned `d098e5bbf9`.

## Next

1. The class→ε-window bridge is not plumbing; it would give uniqueness with no `h⁰ = 1` binder at any degree. Its home is the 7-module closure holding both the mono and two `rep` producers, not a chart file.
2. Price `RelPicSeparatesDivFamZar` at what Abel-chart injectivity costs, undiscounted.

8	/-!
9	# C9b: what `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` of a chart map actually asks for
10	
11	`Picard/Pic0ChartPair.lean` pins `IsChartUniv` — the `hf` half of the `(f, hf)` pair that
12	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes — and its docstring, together with the `c9b` roadmap
13	row, prices it as **one** obligation: the relative form of DAT-C GAP-2 plus the classifier,
14	CERT-Σ-gated.
15	
16	**That pricing is wrong, and this file is the correction.**  `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` is
17	`MorphismProperty.relative` at `yoneda` (mathlib `MorphismProperty/Representable.lean`), and
18	`relative` is *by definition* a conjunction of two independent statements:
19	
20	1. **relative representability** — for every test `T` and every `g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ 𝓟`, the
21	   fibre product of the chart map along `g` is representable *by a scheme*;
22	2. **the property clause** — every represented pullback is an open immersion of schemes.
23	
24	The GAP-2/classifier story is the input to (2) only: it is what makes the fibre a single
25	point, hence the represented pullback an open subscheme.  It says nothing about (1), which
26	is a representability statement about a fibre product.  Read as one clause, a lane waits on
27	CERT-Σ for both halves.  Read as two, half of the work is stateable and provable *now*, with
28	no divisor-representability endpoint and no certificate anywhere in it.
29	
30	## What this file provides, and what it deliberately does not
31	
32	Everything here is stated for an **arbitrary** morphism of big-site presheaves
33	`f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1` and an **arbitrary** open `V ⊆ X`.  No `divRep`
34	endpoint, no certificate, no `Z`, no `θ` and no chart index appears in any statement.  That
35	is the point: `IsChartUniv` becomes *this criterion instantiated at* `abelSigmaChart`, and
36	the divisor-representability shape enters only at the instantiation.
37	
38	The criterion's hypotheses are **elementwise** conditions on the presheaf — a fibrewise
39	injectivity clause and a clause producing the representing open — because that is what
40	mathlib's `MorphismProperty.relative.of_exists` reduces the goal to once the presheaf
41	category's pullbacks are computed pointwise (`Types.isPullback_iff`).
42	
43	## Main declarations
44	
45	* `AlgebraicGeometry.ChartFibrePresented` — the elementwise datum (1) needs: for each test
46	  point `g` of the target, an open `W` of the test and an identification of the `W`-points
47	  with the chart points hitting `g`.  This is the *shape* of a fibre-product presentation,
48	  named so that a producer knows exactly what it owes.
49	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented` — **the criterion**:
50	  a `ChartFibrePresented` datum gives `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f`, discharging BOTH clauses
51	  at once.  Certificate-free and divRep-free.
52	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mono_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf` — the converse direction that makes
53	  the split honest: `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f` *implies* `f` is a monomorphism.  So "the
54	  Abel map is not a monomorphism", which three files cite as the reason the unrestricted
55	  certificate fails, is a consequence of the criterion rather than an extra obligation — and
56	  it shows the elementwise injectivity clause below is **necessary**, not an artefact of
57	  this route.
58	* `AlgebraicGeometry.injective_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf` — the same fact in the
59	  elementwise form a chart-locus argument can actually use.
60	-/
61	
62	set_option autoImplicit false
63	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
64	
65	universe u
66	
67	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
68	
69	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
70	
71	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
72	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
73	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
74	
75	noncomputable section
76	
77	/-! ## The necessary direction: an open immersion of presheaves is a monomorphism
78	
79	Stated first, because it is what tells us the criterion below asks for the right thing. -/
80	
81	/-- **An open immersion of presheaves out of a representable is a monomorphism.**
82	
83	This is mathlib's `presheaf_mono_of_le` at `P := IsOpenImmersion`, whose hypothesis
84	`IsOpenImmersion ≤ monomorphisms Scheme` is the landed `IsOpenImmersion.le_monomorphisms`.
85	
86	Recorded because the whole chart layer rests on the sentence "the Abel map is not a
87	monomorphism, so `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` is false for the unrestricted divisor scheme"
88	(`Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean:54`, repeated in `Pic0ChartPair.lean:14`).  That sentence is a
89	*derivation*, not an independent input, and this lemma is the derivation. -/
90	theorem mono_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf {X : Scheme.{u}}
91	    {f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1} (hf : IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f) :
92	    Mono f :=
93	  MorphismProperty.presheaf_mono_of_le IsOpenImmersion.le_monomorphisms hf
94	
95	/-- **The elementwise form of the necessary direction**: if `f` is an open immersion of
96	presheaves then on every test it is injective on points.
97	
98	This is the clause `ChartFibrePresented.fibre_injective` below, read backwards, and it is
99	why that clause is not an artefact of this particular route: any proof of
100	`IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f` whatsoever yields it.  For the Abel chart it is exactly "the
101	normalized effective representative is unique", i.e. the relative form of DAT-C GAP-2 — so
102	GAP-2 is *forced* by the target, not merely sufficient for it. -/
103	theorem injective_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf {X : Scheme.{u}}
104	    {f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1} (hf : IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f)
105	    (T : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ) :
106	    Function.Injective (f.app T) :=
107	  (mono_iff_injective (f.app T)).mp
108	    ((NatTrans.mono_iff_mono_app f).mp (mono_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf hf) T)
109	
110	/-! ## The sufficient direction: the elementwise datum, and the criterion -/
111	
112	variable (C) in
113	/-- **The fibre of a chart map over one test point, presented by an open of the test.**
114	
115	This is the datum mathlib's `relative.of_exists` asks for at a single
116	`g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ pic0SigmaSheaf C`, written out so a producer can see exactly what it
117	owes.  Given a chart map `f` out of `X`:
118	
119	* `W` is an open subscheme of the test `T` — the locus where the class named by `g` *is* a
120	  chart value.  For the Abel chart this is `chartLocus`;
121	* `r` recovers the chart point: over `W`, the divisor family whose class `g` is;
122	* `sq` says the two ways round agree;
123	* `exists_factor` is the honest content — a test point of `X` and a test point of `T` with
124	  the *same* class come from a unique point of `W`.  Existence is coverage-on-the-locus;
125	  the uniqueness half is *not* a field here, because it is free: `W.ι` is a monomorphism.
126	
127	Nothing in this structure mentions a divisor scheme, a certificate, a twist or a chart
128	index.  It is a statement about a morphism of presheaves and an open of a test. -/
129	structure ChartFibrePresented {X T : Scheme.{u}}
130	    (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) (g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
131	    where
132	  /-- The locus of the test where the class named by `g` is a chart value. -/
133	  W : T.Opens
134	  /-- The chart point over that locus. -/
135	  r : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X
136	  /-- The square commutes: `r` names the class `g` restricted to `W`. -/
137	  sq : yoneda.map r ≫ f = yoneda.map W.ι ≫ g
138	  /-- **Coverage on the locus**: an `S`-point of `X` and an `S`-point of `T` carrying the
139	  same class factor through `W`, compatibly with both projections. -/
140	  exists_factor : ∀ (S : Scheme.{u}) (v : S ⟶ X) (w : S ⟶ T),
141	    f.app (op S) v = g.app (op S) w → ∃ u : S ⟶ (W : Scheme.{u}), u ≫ r = v ∧ u ≫ W.ι = w
142	
143	namespace ChartFibrePresented
144	
145	variable {X T : Scheme.{u}} {f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1}
146	  {g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1}
147	
148	/-- **The datum presents the fibre product**: the square of `ChartFibrePresented` is a
149	pullback of presheaves.
150	
151	Pullbacks in a presheaf category are computed pointwise
152	(`IsPullback.of_forall_isPullback_app`), and a pointwise pullback of types is exactly
153	"commutes + jointly injective + jointly surjective" (`Types.isPullback_iff`).  The first is
154	`sq`, the third is `exists_factor`, and the second is free from `W.ι` being a
155	monomorphism — which is where the openness of `W` does its work. -/
156	theorem isPullback (D : ChartFibrePresented C f g) :
157	    IsPullback (yoneda.map D.r) (yoneda.map D.W.ι) f g := by
158	  refine IsPullback.of_forall_isPullback_app fun S => ?_
159	  rw [Types.isPullback_iff]
160	  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
161	  · exact congrArg (fun φ : yoneda.obj (D.W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1 =>
162	      φ.app S) D.sq
163	  · -- joint injectivity: already forced by `W.ι` alone, being a monomorphism
164	    rintro u₁ u₂ ⟨-, h₂⟩
165	    have : u₁ ≫ D.W.ι = u₂ ≫ D.W.ι := h₂
166	    exact (cancel_mono D.W.ι).mp this
167	  · -- joint surjectivity: `exists_factor` at the test `S.unop`
168	    intro v w hvw
169	    obtain ⟨u, hu₁, hu₂⟩ := D.exists_factor S.unop v w hvw
170	    exact ⟨u, hu₁, hu₂⟩
171	
172	end ChartFibrePresented
173	
174	/-- **THE CRITERION** — `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` from elementwise data, discharging BOTH
175	clauses of `MorphismProperty.relative` at once.
176	
177	Given, for every test point of the target sheaf, a `ChartFibrePresented` datum, the chart map
178	is an open immersion of presheaves.  Certificate-free, divRep-free, and with no reference to
179	divisors: the input is a family of opens of tests together with the coverage statement on
180	each.
181	
182	This is the honest shape of `IsChartUniv`'s obligation.  Reading `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf`
183	as a single "relative GAP-2" statement conflates:
184	
185	* **relative representability** — that the fibre product is a scheme at all.  Supplied here
186	  by `W`, an open subscheme of the test, and proved by `ChartFibrePresented.isPullback`;
187	* **the property clause** — that each represented pullback is an open immersion.  Supplied
188	  here by `W.ι` being an open immersion, which is free.
189	
190	What is *not* free, and is the whole mathematical content, is `exists_factor`: a class that
191	agrees with a chart value must come from the locus.  For the Abel chart that is the relative
192	form of DAT-C GAP-2 (uniqueness of the normalized effective representative) fed through the
193	classifier — so the CERT-Σ gate is real, but it gates ONE field of ONE structure rather than
194	the whole certificate. -/
195	theorem isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented {X : Scheme.{u}}
196	    (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
197	    (D : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1),
198	      ChartFibrePresented C f g) :
199	    IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f := by
200	  refine MorphismProperty.relative.of_exists fun T g => ?_
201	  exact ⟨(D T g).W, yoneda.map (D T g).r, (D T g).W.ι, (D T g).isPullback,
202	    inferInstance⟩
203	
204	/-! ## The criterion is not vacuous
205	
206	A structure whose hard field is an existential can be inhabited for trivial reasons, and a
207	criterion built on one is then worthless.  This section rules that out **by proof** rather
208	than by inspection: the datum is unconstructible exactly when it must be. -/
209	
210	/-- **Non-vacuity of `ChartFibrePresented`, from the necessary direction.**
211	
212	If a chart map fails to be injective on the points of even one test, then no family of
213	`ChartFibrePresented` data exists for it.  In particular the criterion cannot be satisfied
214	for the *unrestricted* Abel chart, whose non-injectivity is the linear system `|D|`
215	(`Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean:54`): the criterion's hypothesis is genuinely as strong as the
216	conclusion, and `exists_factor` is not a clause one can talk one's way past.
217	
218	The proof composes the two halves of this file, which is the point of having both. -/
219	theorem isEmpty_forall_chartFibrePresented_of_not_injective {X : Scheme.{u}}
220	    (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) (T : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ)
221	    (hT : ¬ Function.Injective (f.app T)) :
222	    IsEmpty (∀ (T' : Scheme.{u}) (g : yoneda.obj T' ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1),
223	        ChartFibrePresented C f g) :=
224	  ⟨fun D => hT (injective_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf
225	    (isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented f D) T)⟩
226	
227	/-- The same statement in the form a lane will meet it: the criterion's input **implies**
228	elementwise injectivity on every test.  So a lane that cannot prove uniqueness of the
229	normalized effective representative cannot supply the datum either — the CERT-Σ gate is not
230	an artefact of how `IsChartUniv` was pinned. -/
231	theorem injective_of_chartFibrePresented {X : Scheme.{u}}
232	    (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
233	    (D : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1),
234	      ChartFibrePresented C f g) (T : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ) :
235	    Function.Injective (f.app T) :=
236	  injective_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf
237	    (isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented f D) T
238	
239	end
240	
241	end AlgebraicGeometry

*** CENSUS CORRECTION 2026-07-29, SAME SESSION (review-ajcr, run 0082 s0006), caught by a
fresh-context review of my OWN commit f272fe221. THE COUNT BELOW IS FALSE: ELEVEN DECLARATIONS,
NOT SIX -- and the five I dropped are exactly the PRODUCERS. The DIRECTION finding stands; only
the census sentence was wrong. ***

WHAT I WROTE: "IsPlusHonest has exactly SIX declarations tree-wide (:200 def, .mul :209, .inv
:220, .pow :230, chartLocusOpensOfIsPlusHonest :334, mem_ :343) -- none a spreading-out, a
field-point reduction or a localisation statement."

THE MECHANISM, and it is reusable: I grepped CASE-SENSITIVELY for `IsPlusHonest`. Lean convention
puts a predicate in lowerCamelCase in SUFFIX position, so every producer is named
`..._isPlusHonest` and NONE of them matched. Re-measured case-insensitively, the true census in
Pic0ChartPlusFibreProducer.lean is ELEVEN: add :245 thetaFamily_isPlusHonest, :256
sigmaFamily_isPlusHonest, :275 abelDiv_isPlusHonest, :294 chartTwist_isPlusHonest, and :316
isOpen_chartLocus_of_isPlusHonest.

WHY IT IS NOT COSMETIC. The five I dropped are the four PRODUCERS plus the consumer that pays
CHART-U(b). A census whose entire purpose was "is there a producer of a useful shape" enumerated
only the declarations that CANNOT be that thing, and then read their absence-of-shape as the
shape's absence. The conclusion survives -- I have now read all eleven and none is a spreading-out
or a localisation -- but it survives BY LUCK, and a lane told "six declarations, no producer" might
go build thetaFamily_isPlusHonest, which already exists.

WHAT STANDS, unchanged and re-read from statements: the DIRECTION finding. chartLocus is a
predicate on the IMAGE under picEtMap along Over.testPoint (covariant, free); IsPlusHonest demands
a PREIMAGE under relPicToPicEt at Gamma(T.left, U) (contravariant, the gap). And the genuine
near-miss to cite is NOT an absence at all -- it is PicEtAff.unit_surjective_of_section
(EffectivityClose.lean:141) with .unitEquiv_of_section (:186), already recorded above.

*** SHARPENED 2026-07-29 (review-ajcr, run 0082 s0006), answering ajcr-p2's question on I-0926.
THE OBSTRUCTION IS A DIRECTION, NOT A BASE SHAPE -- so even my corrected "base-shape" wording
below is not the most useful framing. Use this one. ***

p2 asked whether the coverage datum can be reduced to field points, since chartLocus is pointwise
via Over.testPoint: if so, base shape would not bind. MEASURED, from the two statements:

 * chartLocus C m Z lam = {t | IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) (chartTwist ..))}
   (Pic0ChartLocus.lean:244-247). Membership is a predicate on the IMAGE of lam under picEtMap.
   Pushing forward is functorial, so the passage to kappa(t) is FREE. LSP-checked the elaborated
   type at :247: picEt C (overSpec k (Over.testPointField t)).
 * IsPlusHonest C T mu = forall U : T.left.affineOpens, EXISTS z, relPicToPicEt .. z = ..
   (Pic0ChartPlusFibreProducer.lean:200-203). This asks for a PREIMAGE at the ring Gamma(T.left, U).

So the free passage is COVARIANT and the open obligation is CONTRAVARIANT. Knowing the fibre class
lies in relPic's image over the FIELD gives nothing at A: you would need the image to descend along
relPic(A) -> relPic(kappa(t)), which is a spreading-out. MEASURED that no such thing exists:
IsPlusHonest has exactly SIX declarations tree-wide (:200 def, .mul :209, .inv :220, .pow :230,
chartLocusOpensOfIsPlusHonest :334, mem_ :343) -- none a spreading-out, a field-point reduction or a
localisation statement. Zero LSP diagnostics on that file, so the absence is measured, not grepped.

CONSEQUENCE FOR A LANE ON THIS ROW. Do NOT spend a round on "general affine base -> field point";
the missing direction is the descent. What IS a real, self-contained brick, and is genuinely absent
by the census above: a spreading-out lemma for the RANGE of relPicToPicEt along a localisation
A -> A_f. That is the descent in miniature -- not cheap, but bounded and honestly stated.

NOT WEAKENED BY THIS: p2's landed Pic0ChartCoverageAffineTest.lean (chartsCoverLocally_of_affineLocal,
with converse) is a SITE fact and stands on its own; it buys a quantifier, as p2 said themselves.

*** SELF-CORRECTION 2026-07-29, SAME SESSION (review-ajcr, run 0082 s0004, after a fresh-context
review of my own work). THE IsPlusHonest FINDING BELOW IS OVERSTATED ON THE STEP THAT CARRIES IT.
The route-decision conclusion SURVIVES, for a different and better-evidenced reason. ***

WHAT I GOT WRONG. I argued: relPicToPicEt lands in PicEtAff.unit, unit is mk at the TRIVIAL cover
`.self A` alone, therefore honesty asserts that no nontrivial etale cover is needed. That step is
FALSE. PicEtAff.unit_eq_mk (Picard/RelPicCoverInjective.lean:48) proves a unit class is presented on
EVERY cover E, not only on `.self` -- so "mk at the trivial cover" describes one PRESENTATION, not
the RANGE, and nothing follows about which classes the range contains.

/-!
# DAT-B B-5: from pointwise coverage to the sieve condition

`Picard/Pic0ChartLocalSurjectivity.lean` reduced B-6 to `ChartsCoverLocally`, whose statement
is *sieve-theoretic*: for every test `T` and every degree-zero class `s` on it, the supremum
of the per-chart image sieves is a Zariski covering sieve.  The dat-b row calls that "B-5
verbatim" and says a producer discharges it "by exhibiting one open neighbourhood and one
index per point of `T`".

**That last sentence was a claim about a bridge nobody had written.**  What B-5's geometry
produces is pointwise: for each point `t` of the test, an open `W ∋ t`, an index `i`, and a
chart point over `W` whose class restricts to `s`.  What `ChartsCoverLocally` asks for is
membership of a Grothendieck topology.  The two are connected by a *cover construction* —
`Scheme.Cover.mkOfCovers` at the family `{W t}` indexed by the points of `T` — and the
connection is what this file supplies.

## Why the bridge is not bookkeeping the producer can inline

Three things have to line up, and each is a place a lane would stall:

* the cover must be indexed by a type in the right universe.  Indexing by the points of `T`
  works (`↥T : Type u` for `T : Scheme.{u}`) and is the *only* index available before any
  geometry is known — a producer that tries to index by a chosen finite subcover needs
  quasi-compactness, which no row assumes;
* `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff` asks for `Presieve.ofArrows 𝒰.X 𝒰.f ≤ S.arrows`, i.e. a
  statement about the *presieve generated by the cover maps*, so the per-point witness has to
  be produced after destructing `ofArrows` — which binds the point, not an arbitrary map into
  `T`.  This is where the pointwise data is consumed;
* the per-point index makes the target sieve a *supremum*, and `le_iSup` is what turns "some
  chart works at `t`" into "the supremum contains `W t`".  Nothing forces one index to work
  at every point, which is the chart-parameter heterogeneity the dat-b row records — here it
  costs literally nothing, because `iSup` is what the statement already had.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise` — **the bridge**, stated for an
  arbitrary family of sieves: pointwise opens with a per-point index give the supremum sieve
  covering status.  No presheaf, no chart, no `pic⁰`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise` — `ChartsCoverLocally` from exactly the
  data B-5 produces: per test point, an open neighbourhood, an index, and a chart point over
  that open with the right class.  **This is what a coverage lane owes, and nothing more.**
* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_pointwise` — the composite: pointwise
  coverage gives the local-surjectivity instance `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes, i.e.
  B-5 ⟹ B-6 in one step.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.pointwise_of_chartsCoverLocally` — the **converse**, and the reason this
  is a reduction rather than a restatement: the sieve condition gives back an open cover of
  the test on each of whose members some chart hits `s`.  So the pointwise form is not a
  strengthening chosen to be provable.
-/

18	whole certificate.  Concretely, the criterion's `ChartFibrePresented` datum has four fields,
19	and at the Abel chart three of them are supplied here:

22	|---|---|---|
23	| `W` | `chartLocus` of the test point's class, as an open | **shape supplied here**, but at the

41	* `chartLocusOpens` is **constructed**, not hypothesised, so the `W` field is a *shape* a lane

71	exactly the gap).  This file supplies the **`hf`** half — the fibre datum at the restricted
72	chart — and the assembly that consumes both.  Nothing here re-proves either sibling.

76	* **Nothing here produces any input.**  This file replaces a badly-gated route by a
77	  well-gated one; it discharges no antecedent.  `rep` (divisor representability) is a hypothesis

/-!
# THE PRODUCER: `IsChartDatumPlusFibre` for a class in the image of the sheafification unit

## What this file closes

`Picard/Pic0ChartLocusPlusFibre.lean` proves CHART-U(b) at a general test from a per-affine-piece
`IsChartDatumPlusFibre`, and its header says plainly what it does not do:

> The hypothesis is a *per-affine-piece existence of a datum with the plus-class property*, and
> nothing here produces such a datum.

**This file produces one**, and the ingredient that was missing is smaller than four successive
sessions on this leaf priced it: on an **affine** test the canonical field point `Over.testPoint t`
**is** the base-change morphism `overSpecMap A κ(t)`.  Both sides are `Spec` of the same ring map —
`Over.instAlgebraTestPointFieldAffine` is *defined* as `Spec.preimage` of `fromSpecResidueField`,
so `Spec.map_preimage` closes it — but nothing in the tree said so, and every plus-class identity
on this lane is an identity between a class pulled along `Over.testPoint` and one pulled along
`relCurveMap`.  Without the comparison the two sides are not even syntactically comparable; with
it they are the same class.

## The shape of the producer, and its one genuine restriction

`IsChartDatumPlusFibre C π μ D` compares `μ`'s fibre at `κ(t)`, read as a plus class, with the
plus-*unit* of `D`'s fibre class.  So the natural hypothesis on `μ` is that it is *already* a
plus unit — i.e. in the image of the sheafification unit `relPicToPicEt` — and then `D` comes
from `exists_cechPicClass_eq` applied to any Čech representative.

That restriction is real and is named `IsPlusHonest` below.  It is **not** vacuous and **not**
automatic:

* not automatic — a general plus class over `Spec A` is `PicEtAff.mk E x` for an étale cover `E`,
  and `Picard/Pic0ChartHonest.lean` is precisely the record that it becomes honest only over
  `E.Carrier`, not over `A`.  So `IsPlusHonest` is a genuine hypothesis, not a restatement;
* not vacuous, and this is the payoff — the range of `relPicToPicEt` is a **subgroup**, and every
  class the chart layer twists by is in it: the θ-family (`thetaFamily_isPlusHonest`), the
  Σ-family, and the Abel value itself (`abelDiv_isPlusHonest`).  So `chartTwist` preserves
  honesty, and CHART-U(b) becomes **unconditional** on exactly the classes DAT-C's Σ-chart reads.

  **A CORRECTION TO THIS PARAGRAPH, from a fresh-context review of the commit that first wrote
  it, and it is the same failure this leaf recorded one round earlier.**  When first committed the
  sentence above cited `abelDiv_isPlusHonest` **and that declaration did not exist** — a
  workspace-wide grep returned exactly one hit, the sentence itself.  That is precisely the
  failure mode r7 diagnosed (`docstring-declaration-lists-unchecked`) and filed a lesson about,
  reproduced by the very session that filed it, inside its own *non-vacuity* argument.
  A kernel check, a `sorry` census and an axiom probe are all silent about it.

  It also mattered mathematically, which is why it was worth writing rather than deleting: the
  θ- and Σ-witnesses are the **twist factors**, which `chartTwist_isPlusHonest` discharges anyway,
  so they say nothing about the class being *charted*.  Since `chartValue = abelDiv · Σ · (θᵐ)⁻¹`,

  carrying the whole of the final clause.  It is now proved (below), so the paragraph stands as
  written; had it not been, the honest statement would have been "no residue beyond
  `IsPlusHonest lam`", with the Σ-chart clause unproved.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.testPoint_eq_overSpecMap` — **the comparison**: on an affine test the
  canonical field point is the base-change morphism.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.isChartDatumPlusFibre_of_relPicToPicEt` — the producer, with the datum given.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isChartDatumPlusFibre_of_mem_range` — **the producer proper**: for a

* `AlgebraicGeometry.IsPlusHonest` — the per-affine-piece form, closed under the group operations.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpen_chartLocus_of_isPlusHonest` — **CHART-U(b) with no residue** for an

-/

/-- **Heterogeneity costs nothing in the certificate**: the `hf` clause of a mixed-parameter
family is exactly a per-index `IsChartUniv`, by definition of both.

different parameters, with no additional compatibility between them — there is no coherence
condition across indices, because `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` imposes none. -/
theorem isOpenImmersion_presheaf_mixedParamChart {ι : Type u} (nn : ι → ℕ)
    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (nn i : ℤ))
    (V : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens)
    (huniv : ∀ i, IsChartUniv C π (nn i) (rep i) (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i) (V i)) (i : ι) :
    IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V i) :=
  huniv i

variable (C π) in
/-- **A mixed-parameter chart family is admissible input to the DAT-glue seam.**

`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` accepts it verbatim.  This is the statement that settles the
question `Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack` and I-0660 both left implicit: the representability engine
never sees a chart parameter, so the forced calibration `b = n` is a *per-chart* condition and
carries no uniformity obligation.

Note what remains hypothetical here and is not weakened by this: `hf` (i.e. `IsChartUniv`, still
CERT-Σ-gated), local surjectivity (DAT-B B-6), and the *existence* of `rep i` at parameters other
than `g` — which is the question this observation hands to the divisor-representability lane. -/
def mixedParamRepresentableBy {ι : Type u} (nn : ι → ℕ)
    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (nn i : ℤ))
    (V : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens)
    (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V i))
    [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology
      (Sigma.desc (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V))] :
    (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy
      (Over.mk ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv
        (𝟙 (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued)).1) :=
  pic0RepresentableByOfCharts C (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V) hf

end

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartCoveragePointwise

/-!
# B-5 at the Abel chart: what the pointwise datum unfolds to, and what it costs

`Picard/Pic0ChartCoveragePointwise.lean` reduces `ChartsCoverLocally` — hence B-6 — to a
four-part datum at each point of each test.  That reduction is stated for an *arbitrary*
family of presheaf maps, so it says nothing about how hard the datum is at the family that
matters.  This file instantiates it at `abelSigmaChart` and computes the answer.

## The computation, and the one thing it makes visible

A section of `pic0SigmaSheaf C` over a **bare** test scheme `T` is by definition a *pair*
`⟨a, λ⟩` with `a : T ⟶ Spec k` and `λ` a degree-zero class on the slice object `Over.mk a`
(`Over.sigmaExtension`, `Picard/OverSigmaExtension.lean`).  And `(Over.mk a).left` is `T`
itself, definitionally.  So the big-site/slice crossing that looks like it needs a bridge does
not: the pointwise datum's `t : ↥T` *is* a point of the slice test, and `chartLocus` applies to
it with no transport.  `abelChartApp_eq` below records the crossing as an equation rather than
leaving it to unfold at a use site.

What the computation *does* make visible is where the cost sits.  `abelSigmaChart`'s value at
`x : W ⟶ D.left` is `⟨x ≫ D.hom, chartValue … (rep.homEquiv …)⟩`, so matching it against the
restriction of `⟨a, λ⟩` needs **both** components: the Σ-component is an equation between
morphisms to `Spec k`, and only then is there a class equation.  A producer that supplies the
class half alone has not supplied the datum — the Σ-component is what pins the chart point to
lie *over* the test, and it is free only because `W.ι ≫ a` is what `D.hom` must equal.

## THE CORRECTION THIS FILE CARRIES, against this lane's own headline

`Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean:40` says of its `chartLocusOpens`:

> `chartLocusOpens` is **constructed**, not hypothesised — the `W` field costs zero, which is
> a real reduction of the datum from four fields to three

**The second clause is false, and the roadmap `c9b` row repeats it** ("`W` needs nothing").
`chartLocusOpens` takes an argument `haff`, the affine-local openness of the locus at every
affine open of the test, and *nothing in the tree discharges it*:
`isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal'` (`Pic0ChartLocusIsoInvariance.lean`) removed the
`IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant` hypothesis and passes `haff` straight through, as does
`isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal` before it.  The affine case that would feed it is
`isOpen_setOf_isSplitWitness_of_presentation` (`Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen.lean:321`), which is
itself conditional on `IsChartDatumPresentation` — B-4's *named residue*.

**Update, same session** (`Picard/Pic0ChartPresentationConverse.lean`): that residue is now
*entirely witness-free*.  Its forward half already was (the trivial splitting), and its
converse `hconv` — the descent direction, open for three sessions — is discharged by plus-unit
injectivity.  So what `haff` ultimately costs is a `cechPicClass` base-change identity: no
witness, no `H¹`, no divisor, and nothing certificate- or divRep-gated.

So the honest accounting is: **`W` costs `haff`, which costs B-4's presentation residue.**  The
datum went from four fields to three *shapes* but not to three *obligations*.  What is
genuinely free is the type-level crossing above, and `chartLocusHaff` below is the residue
named so it cannot be lost again.

## Main declarations

Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartTwistSplit
import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.DegreeBaseFieldInvariance

/-!
# COV-1 input 2: the DEGREE of the presenting class of the twisted fibre class

`Picard/Pic0ChartTwistSplit.lean` names the Čech class that presents the twisted fibre class
over the splitting field `L`:

  `M₀ · CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L) (chartTwistClass C m Z)`.

`w4-datb` §1.2 steps 2–4 then need its `L`-degree, because that is what decides whether the
class can carry an effective witness with `h¹ = 0` at all: the greedy drop of
`RiemannRoch/CoverageDrop.lean` consumes a divisor of degree `g + e`.

This file computes it, and the computation is exactly the degree ledger the worksheet pins:

  `classDeg L (presenting class) = m·d₁ − deg_k Z`   when `λ` is degree-zero,

so under the chart-index constraint `deg_k Z = m·d₁ − g` it is `+g` — and with the drop budget
`e` folded in (`deg_k Z = m·d₁ − g − e`) it is `g + e`, which is `exists_effective_sub_h0_eq_one`'s
hypothesis on the nose.

## The two halves, and which one is nontrivial

* the **twist factor** is a base class base-changed to `L`, so its `L`-degree is its
  `k`-degree by **E-iv-alg** (`classDeg_cechPicMap_baseFieldTransition`) — no per-field
  ledger constant crosses, which is the I-0204 discipline;
* the **`λ` factor** has `L`-degree zero, and this is where degree-zero-ness is *spent*.
  It is `degAt λ (testPoint) = 0` read through the degree seam: `degAt` of a class whose
  affine collapse is a plus unit of `relPicMk M₀` is `classDeg` of `M₀`
  (`degAt_of_affineEquiv_eq_unit_relPicMk`).

The second half is the reason this file exists rather than being three `rw`s inside COV-1: the
seam from "`μ` is presented over `L` by `M₀`" to "`classDeg L M₀ = degAt μ`" is a statement
about `PicEtAff.map` versus `picEtMap`, not about degrees.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.classDeg_cechPicMap_base_of_field` — the `L`-degree of a base class
  base-changed to `L` is its `k`-degree (E-iv-alg in the `relCurveMap` spelling).
* `AlgebraicGeometry.classDeg_chartTwistClass_baseChange` — the twist factor contributes
  exactly `m·d₁ − deg_k Z`.
-/

1	/-

4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors
5	-/
6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartCoveragePointwise
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartUnivReduce
8	
9	/-!
10	# The coupling of the atlas open to the coverage witness
11	
12	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` (`Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161`) has three antecedents, and
13	the board tracks them on three separate rows: `IsChartUniv` (c9b), Zariski-local surjectivity
14	of `Sigma.desc f` (dat-b B-6), and `rep i` (divrep).  Reading those rows one concludes the
15	three compose — discharge each and the seam fires.
16	
17	**They do not compose as stated.**  The atlas the seam consumes is a family of *restricted*
18	charts `restrictChart (abelSigmaChart …) (V i)` (`Picard/Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree.lean:86`),
19	whose source is `(V i : Scheme)` — an open of the *chart source*, i.e. of the divisor scheme.
20	So the coverage antecedent, unfolded through `chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise`
21	(`Pic0ChartCoveragePointwise.lean:128`), must produce a chart point
22	`x : (W : Scheme) ⟶ (V i : Scheme)` landing **in that same `V i`**, while coverage geometry
23	produces a point of the divisor scheme `D.left` with no such constraint.  The two opens the
24	route wants to identify live on different objects — `V i` on the divisor scheme, `chartLocus`
25	on the test — and no declaration in the tree relates them.
26	
27	That is an obligation *between* two antecedents, owned by no row, and it is why "close c9b,
28	then close B-6" would not have composed even with both closed.
29	
30	## What this file does about it
31	
32	It names the coupling and derives restricted coverage from unrestricted coverage together
33	with a range containment: the coverage witness, viewed in the chart source, factors
34	set-theoretically through `V i`.  Given that, the witness lifts to `V i` along the open
35	immersion `(V i).ι` by `IsOpenImmersion.lift`, and the class it names is unchanged because
36	`restrictChart` is *by definition* precomposition with `yoneda.map (V i).ι` — so the lift's
37	chart value is the unlifted one, with no transport.
38	
39	**THREE CORRECTIONS TO AN EARLIER DRAFT OF THIS HEADER**, all from a fresh-context audit
40	(2026-07-29, inbox `I-0894`), because each would have mispriced the row:
41	
42	1. the hypothesis is **NOT "weaker than either antecedent"**, as the draft claimed.  It is the
43	   unrestricted coverage datum **conjoined** with the containment, so it *implies* the
44	   coverage antecedent and is strictly STRONGER than it.  What is true is the much smaller
45	   claim that the containment is all that separates unrestricted from restricted coverage;
46	2. `liftPointwiseToOpens` and `pointwise_of_pointwise_restrictChart` together are one
47	   **biconditional**, and its transport step (`restrictChart_app_apply`) is `rfl`.  So this
48	   file is a *repackaging with its difference named*, and **it closes no gate**.  It is
49	   reported as routing information, not as progress on any antecedent;
50	3. the draft argued about "`V i = chartLocus`" in two places.  **Those carriers do not meet**:
51	   `V i : (X i).Opens` is an open of the chart source (the divisor scheme), while
52	   `chartLocus C m Z lam : Set ↥T.left` is a set on a *test*.  The only bridge is
53	   `chartLocusOpens`, which lands in `T.left.Opens` and costs `haff` (= dat-b's B-4).  The
54	   mismatch is precisely what this file was written to expose, so reasoning as though the two
55	   were interchangeable — as the draft did below — defeated the purpose.
56	
57	What survives all three: the containment is genuine content (probes below), it is exactly the
58	difference between the two coverage statements (the converse), and no declaration in the tree
59	relates the two carriers.
60	
61	## Main declarations
62	
63	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PointwiseCoverage` — the pointwise coverage datum of B-5, named for an
64	  arbitrary chart family so the two atlases (unrestricted, restricted) can be compared.
65	* `AlgebraicGeometry.liftPointwiseToOpens` — **the coupling**: pointwise coverage for a family
66	  `f` plus the range containment gives pointwise coverage for the *restricted* family
67	  `fun i => restrictChart (f i) (V i)`.
68	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallySurjective_restrictChart_of_pointwise` — the composite into the
69	  instance the seam consumes, for the restricted atlas.
70	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pointwise_of_pointwise_restrictChart` — the **converse**: restricted
71	  coverage gives unrestricted coverage *and* the containment.  So `hV` is not a hypothesis
72	  chosen for provability — it is exactly the difference between the two, and a lane cannot
73	  reach the restricted atlas while avoiding it.
74	-/
75

92	/-- **The pointwise coverage datum of B-5**, named.
93	
94	This is verbatim the hypothesis of `chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise`
95	(`Pic0ChartCoveragePointwise.lean:128`), given a name so that the same statement can be
96	compared at two different chart families — which is the whole point of this file: B-6 is
97	consumed at the *restricted* atlas, while coverage geometry produces the datum at the
98	*unrestricted* one. -/

104	
105	/-! ## The chart value of a restricted chart at a lifted point -/
106	
107	/-- **A restricted chart reads a lifted point exactly as the unrestricted chart reads the
108	point itself.**
109	
110	`restrictChart f V` is `yoneda.map V.ι ≫ f` by definition, so its value at `u` is the value
111	of `f` at `u ≫ V.ι`.  No transport, no naturality of `f` — the composition is on the source
112	side, where `yoneda.map` is precomposition.
113

`Picard/DivRepClassifyZar.lean` proves the *hom* side of the backward classification:
a locally certified divisor class determines a **unique** morphism satisfying the
characterizing clause (`isDivRepClassify_unique`).  This file proves the *class* side:
a morphism satisfying the clause determines the **class**.

  `grPair` pull the tautological pair back equally.  The forward implication is

  (`Picard/GrassmannianPairCompare.lean`); the converse is the two chart-compatibility
  theorems of `Picard/DivCarvePairChart.lean` read in the `pairTaut` spelling.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.eq_of_isDivRepClassify` — **the separation theorem**: two locally
  certified divisor classes over an affine test whose classifying morphism is the same

composite certificate × frame cover (`DivFamZar.exists_certChartCover`), the frame
transport `map_window_frame_toSubmodule`, the seam-free relative mono

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom π]
variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]

noncomputable section

variable (C π) in
/-- **A chart family whose chart parameter varies with the index.**

Each index `i` carries its own degree parameter `nn i`, its own representing object `D i` of
`divFunctor C π (nn i)`, its own twist exponent `m i` and chart index `Z i` — the latter legal
*at `nn i`*, i.e. `deg_k (Z i) = (m i)·d₁ − nn i`, which is what `chartValue_mem_pic0Subgroup`
requires for that index's chart value to land in `pic⁰`.

The construction is just `restrictChart` of `abelSigmaChart` applied pointwise; the content is
that it *typechecks*, i.e. that the target `pic0SigmaSheaf C` is parameter-free. -/
def mixedParamChart {ι : Type u} (nn : ι → ℕ)
    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (nn i : ℤ))
    (V : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens) (i : ι) :
    yoneda.obj ((V i : Scheme.{u})) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1 :=
  restrictChart (abelSigmaChart C π (nn i) (rep i) (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i)) (V i)

95	`restrictedChartFibre_bot`, leaving the `IsLocallySurjective` instance binder as the sole
96	remaining antecedent.  `not_coverageContainment_bot` constrains the `hcov` *spelling* of coverage,
97	not that instance binder — so it does not by itself rule out a `⊥`-based route through the
98	instance version.
99	
100	**That loophole is now shut, from two directions, and neither is in this file.**
101	
102	* `Picard/Pic0ChartVMonotone.lean`'s `isLocallySurjective_of_bot`: antecedent 2 is *monotone* in
103	  `V`, so inhabiting the instance binder at `⊥` yields it at every `V` and hence for the
104	  **unrestricted** atlas.  The `⊥` route is therefore not cheap — it costs the full coverage
105	  obligation.  (Same file: coverage at *any* `V` implies unrestricted coverage, so the restriction
106	  relieves this side by nothing at all.)
107	* Independently, inbox `I-1049` refutes the instance binder at `⊥` outright, for an arbitrary
108	  chart family.
109	
110	So both endpoints are now refuted at *instance* level rather than at the level of one
111	formulation, and the conditional below ("any `V` that works must be a proper intermediate open")
112	no longer rests on the `hcov` spelling.  It remains a conditional: no `V` is exhibited.
113	
114	**What is still NOT closed, stated plainly.**  `rep` remains a hypothesis with no producer, so
115	`IsChartUniv` is not even statable without it; `hcov` at a useful `V` has no producer; and
116	nothing here produces a chart at a `V` other than `⊥`.  No antecedent of
117	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` is discharged by this file.  What is discharged is the
118	*satisfiability question* about the class, plus the sharp localisation of the remaining
119	obligation.
120	-/

138	/-! ## The empty test, from the sheaf axiom -/
139	
140	/-- **The Σ-sheaf is trivial on an empty test** — by the sheaf axiom, not by any property of
141	`picEt`.
142	
143	The empty sieve covers an empty scheme (`Scheme.bot_mem_grothendieckTopology`), and a sheaf's
144	value at an object with a `⊥` cover is terminal (`Sheaf.isTerminalOfBotCover`); a terminal
145	object of `Type u` is a subsingleton.
146	
147	This is the declaration `Pic0ChartRestrictedFibre.lean` priced as "the triviality of `picEt`
148	over the empty scheme: true, a genuinely separate lemma, and absent from the tree".  Note what
149	does *not* appear: no `picEt`, no `pic0Subgroup`, no `relPic`, no curve geometry.  The residue
150	was named after a `congr 1` had already thrown away the structure that makes it free. -/
151	theorem pic0Sigma_obj_subsingleton_of_isEmpty (S : Scheme.{u}) [IsEmpty S] :
152	    Subsingleton ((pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op S)) :=
153	  (Equiv.subsingleton_congr
154	    ((Types.isTerminalEquivIsoPUnit _
155	      (Sheaf.isTerminalOfBotCover (pic0SigmaSheaf C) S
156	        (Scheme.bot_mem_grothendieckTopology S))).toEquiv)).mpr inferInstance
157	
158	/-- The carrier of the bottom open of a scheme is empty.  Stated as an instance because the
159	`isInitialOfIsEmpty` applications below need it by synthesis. -/
160	instance isEmpty_coe_bot_opens (T : Scheme.{u}) : IsEmpty ((⊥ : T.Opens) : Scheme.{u}) :=
161	  ⟨fun x => x.2⟩
162	
163	/-! ## Inhabitation of the restricted datum -/
164	
165	/-- **`RestrictedChartFibre` at `V = ⊥` is inhabited, with no hypotheses beyond the data the
166	statement mentions.**
167	
168	Take `W := ⊥` as well.  Then:
169	
170	* `r` is the unique map out of an empty scheme (`isInitialOfIsEmpty`);
171	* `sq` is an equality of natural transformations out of `yoneda.obj ↑⊥`; after `ext S x` the
172	  morphism `x : S.unop ⟶ ↑⊥` forces `S.unop` empty, and
173	  `pic0Sigma_obj_subsingleton_of_isEmpty` closes it;
174	* `exists_factor` is free: `v : S ⟶ ↑⊥` forces `S` empty, hence initial, so the factoring map
175	  and both compatibilities are unique.
176	
177	**Why this is worth landing rather than just knowing.**  `Pic0ChartRestrictedFibre.lean` said a
178	lane picking up that row "should produce that witness first … it decides whether the repair is
179	real".  It does, and the answer is yes: the class is not empty, so the repaired route to
180	`IsChartUniv` is not a route to an uninhabitable hypothesis. -/
181	theorem restrictedChartFibre_bot {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
182	    (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
183	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
184	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
185	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ)) :
186	    RestrictedChartFibre C π n rep m Z hdeg ⊥ := by
187	  intro T g
188	  refine ⟨⟨⊥, isInitialOfIsEmpty.to _, ?_, ?_⟩⟩
189	  · ext S x

Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEtCoverBridge
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.OverSigmaExtension
import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Sites.Representability

/-!
# The big-site Zariski sheaf `pic⁰` and the 01JJ seam (DAT-6, stage 3)

The slice trick assembled: the Σ-extension of the degree-zero Picard functor is an
honest sheaf for the big Zariski topology on `Scheme`, and mathlib's 01JJ
local-representability engine applied to it descends to a representation of the
degree-zero Picard functor itself on the slice.

* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0TypeFunctor C`: the degree-zero Picard functor with values in
  types — the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` massage of `pic0Functor`, owned here once
  (`pic0TypeFunctor_obj`/`pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply` are `rfl`).
* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0SigmaFunctor C : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u`: the Σ-extension
  `T ↦ Σ (a : T ⟶ Spec k), pic⁰(Over.mk a)` — the big-site carrier.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf` / **`pic0SigmaSheaf C`**: the sheaf
  certificate.  By mathlib's own reduction the big-site sheaf condition collapses to
  elementwise ∃!-amalgamation on honest open covers
  (`Precoverage.isSheaf_toGrothendieck_iff_of_isStableUnderBaseChange`,
  `exists_cover_of_mem_pretopology`, `Presieve.isSheafFor_arrows_iff` — the
  `BigZariski` TODO is never touched): the Σ-components glue by
  `Scheme.Cover.glueMorphisms`, the fibre components glue by the DAT-6 stage-1
  evaluation bridge (`pic0Subgroup_existsUnique_of_cover`), and the two layers are
  stitched by the stage-2 amalgamation seam (`sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff`) and
  compatibility descent (`map_eq_of_sigmaExtension_map_eq`).
* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`: **the DAT-glue seam** — given a
  chart family of relatively representable open immersions into `pic0SigmaSheaf`
  (DAT-C) that is jointly locally surjective (DAT-B), mathlib's
  `Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy` produces a representation of the
  Σ-extension by the glued scheme, and the stage-2 Σ-descent `overSlice` turns it
  into a representation of `pic0TypeFunctor C` by the glued scheme over the
  Σ-component of the universal element.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

/-! ## The type-valued degree-zero Picard functor -/

/-- The degree-zero Picard functor with values in types: the `forget₂ ⋙ forget`
massage of `pic0Functor`, owned here once for the Σ-extension statements. -/
noncomputable abbrev pic0TypeFunctor : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u :=
  (pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) ⋙ forget GrpCat

      pic0Map C gi ((x i).2) = pic0Map C gj ((x j).2) := by
    intro i j Z gi gj hg
    have hleft : gi.left ≫ 𝓤.f i = gj.left ≫ 𝓤.f j := congrArg Over.Hom.left hg
    have hdesc := Over.map_eq_of_sigmaExtension_map_eq gi gj
      (hx i j Z.left gi.left gj.left hleft)
    rwa [pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply, pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply] at hdesc
  -- glue the fibre components by the stage-1 evaluation bridge
  obtain ⟨s, hs, hsu⟩ := pic0Subgroup_existsUnique_of_cover
    (fun i => (Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY))
    hcov (fun i => (x i).2) hcompat
  refine ⟨⟨aY, s⟩, fun i => ?_, ?_⟩
  · -- the glued Σ-element restricts to the members
    refine (Over.sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff (𝓤.f i) (ha i) s ((x i).2)).mpr ?_
    rw [pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply]
    exact hs i
  · -- uniqueness: Σ-components by `hom_ext`, fibres by bridge separation
    rintro ⟨a', s'⟩ ht'
    obtain rfl : aY = a' := 𝓤.hom_ext aY a' fun i =>
      (ha i).trans (congrArg Sigma.fst (ht' i) : 𝓤.f i ≫ a' = (x i).1).symm
    refine congrArg (Sigma.mk aY) (hsu s' fun i => ?_)
    have hmem := (Over.sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff (𝓤.f i) (ha i) s' ((x i).2)).mp
      (ht' i)
    rwa [pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply] at hmem

/-- **The Σ-extension of the degree-zero Picard functor, bundled as a sheaf on the
big Zariski site** — the object mathlib's 01JJ local-representability engine
consumes. -/
noncomputable def pic0SigmaSheaf : Sheaf Scheme.zariskiTopology.{u} (Type u) :=
  ⟨pic0SigmaFunctor C,
    (isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_of_type _ _).mpr (pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf C)⟩

/-! ## The DAT-glue seam -/

/-- **The DAT-glue statement (worksheet §4, DAT-glue row)**: a chart family of
relatively representable open immersions into the Σ-extension sheaf (DAT-C's
certificates) that is jointly Zariski-locally surjective (DAT-B's coverage) induces —
through mathlib's 01JJ engine and the stage-2 Σ-descent — a representation of the
type-valued degree-zero Picard functor by the glued scheme placed over the
Σ-component of the universal element.  The represented object's `.left` is
`(Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued` and its `.hom` is the universal
element's Σ-component, both definitionally. -/
noncomputable def pic0RepresentableByOfCharts
    {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
    (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i))
    [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)] :
    (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy
      (Over.mk ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv
        (𝟙 (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued)).1) :=
  (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).overSlice

end AlgebraicGeometry

1	/-
2	Copyright (c) 2026 The AlgebraicJacobian authors. All rights reserved.
3	Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors
5	-/
6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartLocalSurjectivity
7	
8	/-!
9	# DAT-B B-5: from pointwise coverage to the sieve condition
10	
11	`Picard/Pic0ChartLocalSurjectivity.lean` reduced B-6 to `ChartsCoverLocally`, whose statement
12	is *sieve-theoretic*: for every test `T` and every degree-zero class `s` on it, the supremum
13	of the per-chart image sieves is a Zariski covering sieve.  The dat-b row calls that "B-5
14	verbatim" and says a producer discharges it "by exhibiting one open neighbourhood and one
15	index per point of `T`".
16	
17	**That last sentence was a claim about a bridge nobody had written.**  What B-5's geometry
18	produces is pointwise: for each point `t` of the test, an open `W ∋ t`, an index `i`, and a
19	chart point over `W` whose class restricts to `s`.  What `ChartsCoverLocally` asks for is
20	membership of a Grothendieck topology.  The two are connected by a *cover construction* —
21	`Scheme.Cover.mkOfCovers` at the family `{W t}` indexed by the points of `T` — and the
22	connection is what this file supplies.
23	
24	## Why the bridge is not bookkeeping the producer can inline
25	
26	Three things have to line up, and each is a place a lane would stall:
27	
28	* the cover must be indexed by a type in the right universe.  Indexing by the points of `T`
29	  works (`↥T : Type u` for `T : Scheme.{u}`) and is the *only* index available before any
30	  geometry is known — a producer that tries to index by a chosen finite subcover needs
31	  quasi-compactness, which no row assumes;
32	* `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff` asks for `Presieve.ofArrows 𝒰.X 𝒰.f ≤ S.arrows`, i.e. a
33	  statement about the *presieve generated by the cover maps*, so the per-point witness has to
34	  be produced after destructing `ofArrows` — which binds the point, not an arbitrary map into
35	  `T`.  This is where the pointwise data is consumed;
36	* the per-point index makes the target sieve a *supremum*, and `le_iSup` is what turns "some
37	  chart works at `t`" into "the supremum contains `W t`".  Nothing forces one index to work
38	  at every point, which is the chart-parameter heterogeneity the dat-b row records — here it
39	  costs literally nothing, because `iSup` is what the statement already had.
40	
41	## Main declarations
42	
43	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise` — **the bridge**, stated for an
44	  arbitrary family of sieves: pointwise opens with a per-point index give the supremum sieve
45	  covering status.  No presheaf, no chart, no `pic⁰`.
46	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise` — `ChartsCoverLocally` from exactly the
47	  data B-5 produces: per test point, an open neighbourhood, an index, and a chart point over
48	  that open with the right class.  **This is what a coverage lane owes, and nothing more.**
49	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_pointwise` — the composite: pointwise
50	  coverage gives the local-surjectivity instance `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes, i.e.
51	  B-5 ⟹ B-6 in one step.
52	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pointwise_of_chartsCoverLocally` — the **converse**, and the reason this
53	  is a reduction rather than a restatement: the sieve condition gives back an open cover of
54	  the test on each of whose members some chart hits `s`.  So the pointwise form is not a
55	  strengthening chosen to be provable.
56	-/
57	
58	set_option autoImplicit false
59	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
60	
61	universe u
62	
63	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
64	
65	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
66	
67	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
68	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
69	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
70	
71	noncomputable section
72	
73	/-! ## The bridge, with no chart content
74	
75	Stated for an arbitrary family of sieves on an arbitrary scheme, because that is all it uses:
76	the coverage half of B-5 is a statement about the *site*, and mixing it with the presheaf
77	statement is what made it look gated. -/
78	
79	/-- **Pointwise data gives a covering supremum sieve.**
80	
81	If every point `t` of `T` has an open neighbourhood `W t` and an index `idx t` such that the
82	inclusion `(W t).ι` lies in the `idx t`-th sieve, then the supremum of the family is a
83	Zariski covering sieve of `T`.
84	
85	The proof is the cover `{W t}_{t : ↥T}` — jointly surjective because `t ∈ W t`, open
86	immersions because they are opens inclusions — fed to `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff`, and
87	then `le_iSup` at the index of the destructed point.
88	
89	Note there is **no compatibility condition between different points**: `idx` is an arbitrary
90	function.  That is why chart-parameter heterogeneity (dat-b row, `Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree`)
91	costs nothing here — a supremum sieve never asks its members to agree. -/
92	theorem mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {T : Scheme.{u}}
93	    (Sv : ι → Sieve T) (W : ↥T → T.Opens) (hW : ∀ t, t ∈ W t) (idx : ↥T → ι)
94	    (hmem : ∀ t, (Sv (idx t)).arrows (W t).ι) :
95	    (⨆ i, Sv i) ∈ Scheme.zariskiTopology T := by
96	  refine Scheme.mem_grothendieckTopology_iff.mpr
97	    ⟨Scheme.Cover.mkOfCovers (↥T) (fun t => (W t : Scheme.{u})) (fun t => (W t).ι)
98	      (fun t => ⟨t, ⟨t, hW t⟩, rfl⟩) (fun t => inferInstance), ?_⟩
99	  rintro V g ⟨t⟩
100	  exact le_iSup Sv (idx t) _ (hmem t)
101	
102	/-! ## `ChartsCoverLocally` from what B-5 actually produces -/
103	
104	variable (C) in
105	/-- **THE B-5 PACKAGING**: `ChartsCoverLocally` from pointwise coverage.
106	
107	The hypothesis is exactly the shape the coverage geometry delivers, and is worth reading
108	field by field against `w4-datb` §1.2.  For every test `T`, every degree-zero class `s` on
109	it, and every point `t` of `T`:
110	
111	* `W` — an open neighbourhood of `t`.  In the intended instantiation this is
112	  `chartLocusOpens` (`Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean`), whose openness is CHART-U(b) and is
113	  unconditional since `IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant` was discharged;
114	* `i` — the chart index, chosen *at `t`*.  Per-point by construction, which is what the
115	  I-0204 non-uniformity of the twist exponent `m` requires;
116	* `x` — a point of the `i`-th chart scheme over `W`, i.e. the divisor family the coverage
117	  argument produces at the splitting field of `κ(t)`;
118	* `hx` — that its class is `s` restricted to `W`.
119	
120	Given that, the sieve condition holds.  So a coverage lane never has to mention `Sigma.desc`,
121	a coproduct of yoneda presheaves, a covering sieve, or a Grothendieck topology: it produces
122	four things at a point and this lemma does the rest.
123	
124	**What this does not do.**  It does not produce the pointwise data — that is B-5's geometry
125	and its residue (the chart-parameter/threshold reconciliation) is recorded on the dat-b row.
126	It removes the site-theoretic layer between that geometry and B-6, which had never been
127	written down and which the row described as though it were already there. -/
128	theorem chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
129	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
130	    (h : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
131	      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
132	        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s) :
133	    ChartsCoverLocally C f := by
134	  intro T s
135	  choose W hW i x hx using h T s
136	  exact mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise _ W hW i fun t => ⟨x t, hx t⟩
137	
138	variable (C) in
139	/-- **B-5 ⟹ B-6 in one step**: pointwise coverage gives the local-surjectivity instance.
140	
141	The composite of `chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise` with `isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc`.
142	Recorded because it is the statement a lane closing coverage wants to cite: the *only*
143	remaining input to the `[Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)]`
144	instance that three files carry as an unproduced `variable` is the pointwise data above. -/
145	theorem isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
146	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
147	    (h : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
148	      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
149	        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s) :
150	    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f) :=
151	  isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc f (chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise C f h)
152	
153	/-! ## The converse: the pointwise form is not a strengthening
154	
155	A reduction whose hypothesis is strictly stronger than its conclusion is a weakening in
156	disguise, and the memory `reduction-needs-its-converse` is about exactly this failure.  Here
157	the converse holds — modulo the one difference that is genuinely there and is named. -/
158	
159	variable (C) in
160	/-- **`ChartsCoverLocally` gives back an open cover on whose members a chart hits `s`.**
161	
162	The converse direction, and the check that the pointwise hypothesis above is the right one.
163	From the sieve condition one extracts a Zariski cover of `T` by `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff`
164	and reads the supremum membership at each cover map.
165	
166	**The one honest difference**, and it is why this is stated with a general `Y ⟶ T` rather than
167	an open of `T`: `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff` returns a cover by *arbitrary* schemes with
168	open-immersion maps, not by opens of `T`.  Those are the same up to isomorphism
169	(`Scheme.Hom.isoOpensRange`) but not on the nose, so the converse produces a cover map where
170	the hypothesis consumed an opens inclusion.  For the purpose this serves — showing the
171	pointwise data is *available*, hence not a hypothesis chosen for provability — a cover map is
172	exactly as good, and pretending otherwise would need a transport that adds nothing. -/
173	theorem pointwise_of_chartsCoverLocally {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
174	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
175	    (h : ChartsCoverLocally C f) (T : Scheme.{u})
176	    (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) :
177	    ∃ (𝒰 : T.Cover.{u} (Scheme.precoverage @IsOpenImmersion)),
178	      ∀ j : 𝒰.I₀, ∃ (i : ι) (x : 𝒰.X j ⟶ X i),
179	        (f i).app (op (𝒰.X j)) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (𝒰.f j).op s := by
180	  obtain ⟨𝒰, hle⟩ := Scheme.mem_grothendieckTopology_iff.mp (h T s)
181	  refine ⟨𝒰, fun j => ?_⟩
182	  have hj := hle (𝒰.X j) (𝒰.f j) (Presieve.ofArrows.mk j)
183	  rw [iSup, Sieve.sSup_apply] at hj
184	  obtain ⟨S, ⟨i, rfl⟩, x, hx⟩ := hj
185	  exact ⟨i, x, hx⟩
186	
187	end
188	
189	end AlgebraicGeometry

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartCoveragePointwise
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartUnivReduce
8	
9	/-!
10	# The coupling of the atlas open to the coverage witness
11	
12	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` (`Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161`) has three antecedents, and
13	the board tracks them on three separate rows: `IsChartUniv` (c9b), Zariski-local surjectivity
14	of `Sigma.desc f` (dat-b B-6), and `rep i` (divrep).  Reading those rows one concludes the
15	three compose — discharge each and the seam fires.
16	
17	**They do not compose as stated.**  The atlas the seam consumes is a family of *restricted*
18	charts `restrictChart (abelSigmaChart …) (V i)` (`Picard/Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree.lean:86`),
19	whose source is `(V i : Scheme)` — an open of the *chart source*, i.e. of the divisor scheme.
20	So the coverage antecedent, unfolded through `chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise`
21	(`Pic0ChartCoveragePointwise.lean:128`), must produce a chart point
22	`x : (W : Scheme) ⟶ (V i : Scheme)` landing **in that same `V i`**, while coverage geometry
23	produces a point of the divisor scheme `D.left` with no such constraint.  The two opens the
24	route wants to identify live on different objects — `V i` on the divisor scheme, `chartLocus`
25	on the test — and no declaration in the tree relates them.
26	
27	That is an obligation *between* two antecedents, owned by no row, and it is why "close c9b,
28	then close B-6" would not have composed even with both closed.
29	
30	## What this file does about it
31	
32	It names the coupling and derives restricted coverage from unrestricted coverage together
33	with a range containment: the coverage witness, viewed in the chart source, factors
34	set-theoretically through `V i`.  Given that, the witness lifts to `V i` along the open
35	immersion `(V i).ι` by `IsOpenImmersion.lift`, and the class it names is unchanged because
36	`restrictChart` is *by definition* precomposition with `yoneda.map (V i).ι` — so the lift's
37	chart value is the unlifted one, with no transport.
38	
39	**THREE CORRECTIONS TO AN EARLIER DRAFT OF THIS HEADER**, all from a fresh-context audit
40	(2026-07-29, inbox `I-0894`), because each would have mispriced the row:
41	
42	1. the hypothesis is **NOT "weaker than either antecedent"**, as the draft claimed.  It is the
43	   unrestricted coverage datum **conjoined** with the containment, so it *implies* the
44	   coverage antecedent and is strictly STRONGER than it.  What is true is the much smaller
45	   claim that the containment is all that separates unrestricted from restricted coverage;
46	2. `liftPointwiseToOpens` and `pointwise_of_pointwise_restrictChart` together are one
47	   **biconditional**, and its transport step (`restrictChart_app_apply`) is `rfl`.  So this
48	   file is a *repackaging with its difference named*, and **it closes no gate**.  It is
49	   reported as routing information, not as progress on any antecedent;
50	3. the draft argued about "`V i = chartLocus`" in two places.  **Those carriers do not meet**:
51	   `V i : (X i).Opens` is an open of the chart source (the divisor scheme), while
52	   `chartLocus C m Z lam : Set ↥T.left` is a set on a *test*.  The only bridge is
53	   `chartLocusOpens`, which lands in `T.left.Opens` and costs `haff` (= dat-b's B-4).  The
54	   mismatch is precisely what this file was written to expose, so reasoning as though the two
55	   were interchangeable — as the draft did below — defeated the purpose.
56	
57	What survives all three: the containment is genuine content (probes below), it is exactly the
58	difference between the two coverage statements (the converse), and no declaration in the tree
59	relates the two carriers.
60	
61	## Main declarations
62	
63	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PointwiseCoverage` — the pointwise coverage datum of B-5, named for an
64	  arbitrary chart family so the two atlases (unrestricted, restricted) can be compared.
65	* `AlgebraicGeometry.liftPointwiseToOpens` — **the coupling**: pointwise coverage for a family
66	  `f` plus the range containment gives pointwise coverage for the *restricted* family
67	  `fun i => restrictChart (f i) (V i)`.
68	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallySurjective_restrictChart_of_pointwise` — the composite into the
69	  instance the seam consumes, for the restricted atlas.
70	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pointwise_of_pointwise_restrictChart` — the **converse**: restricted
71	  coverage gives unrestricted coverage *and* the containment.  So `hV` is not a hypothesis
72	  chosen for provability — it is exactly the difference between the two, and a lane cannot
73	  reach the restricted atlas while avoiding it.
74	-/
75	
76	set_option autoImplicit false
77	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
78	
79	universe u
80	
81	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
82	
83	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
84	
85	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
86	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
87	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
88	
89	noncomputable section
90	
91	variable (C) in
92	/-- **The pointwise coverage datum of B-5**, named.
93	
94	This is verbatim the hypothesis of `chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise`
95	(`Pic0ChartCoveragePointwise.lean:128`), given a name so that the same statement can be
96	compared at two different chart families — which is the whole point of this file: B-6 is
97	consumed at the *restricted* atlas, while coverage geometry produces the datum at the
98	*unrestricted* one. -/
99	def PointwiseCoverage {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
100	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) : Prop :=
101	  ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
102	    ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
103	      (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s
104	
105	/-! ## The chart value of a restricted chart at a lifted point -/
106	
107	/-- **A restricted chart reads a lifted point exactly as the unrestricted chart reads the
108	point itself.**
109	
110	`restrictChart f V` is `yoneda.map V.ι ≫ f` by definition, so its value at `u` is the value
111	of `f` at `u ≫ V.ι`.  No transport, no naturality of `f` — the composition is on the source
112	side, where `yoneda.map` is precomposition.
113	
114	This is the entire reason the coupling below is cheap, and it is worth isolating: a lane that
115	expected the two chart values to differ by a restriction map would look for a compatibility
116	that is not needed. -/
117	lemma restrictChart_app_apply {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
118	    (V : X.Opens) {S : Scheme.{u}} (u : S ⟶ (V : Scheme.{u})) :
119	    (restrictChart f V).app (op S) u = f.app (op S) (u ≫ V.ι) :=
120	  rfl
121	
122	/-! ## The coupling -/
123	
124	variable (C) in
125	/-- **THE COUPLING**: pointwise coverage for `f` plus a range containment gives pointwise
126	coverage for the restricted family.
127	
128	The containment is the honest content: at the point, index and witness coverage produces, the
129	witness's image in the chart source lies inside `V i`.  Everything else is the lift along the
130	open immersion `(V i).ι` and `restrictChart_app_apply`, which is `rfl` — so this direction
131	carries no mathematics beyond the lift, and together with its converse below it is a
132	biconditional rather than a reduction.  **It closes no gate.**
133	
134	Note the shape of the hypothesis: it quantifies over the data coverage *returns*, not over all
135	opens or all witnesses.  So a producer discharges it exactly where it produces the witness,
136	which is the only place the information is available; a formulation asking for the containment
137	uniformly over all witnesses would be strictly stronger.
138	
139	What the containment *means* geometrically depends on which open `V i` is, and this file
140	deliberately does not assume an answer — in particular `V i` is an open of the chart source
141	while `chartLocus` is a set on a test, so the two are not interchangeable and the intended
142	instantiation still owes the `chartLocusOpens` bridge (cost: `haff`, i.e. dat-b's B-4). -/
143	theorem liftPointwiseToOpens {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
144	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) (V : ∀ i, (X i).Opens)
145	    (h : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
146	      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
147	        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s ∧
148	          Set.range (x.base) ⊆ Set.range ((V i).ι.base)) :
149	    PointwiseCoverage C (fun i => restrictChart (f i) (V i)) := by
150	  intro T s t
151	  obtain ⟨W, htW, i, x, hx, hrange⟩ := h T s t
152	  refine ⟨W, htW, i, IsOpenImmersion.lift ((V i).ι) x hrange, ?_⟩
153	  rw [restrictChart_app_apply, IsOpenImmersion.lift_fac]
154	  exact hx
155	
156	variable (C) in
157	/-- **The composite**: coverage plus the containment gives the local-surjectivity instance
158	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes *at the restricted atlas* — which is the atlas
159	`mixedParamRepresentableBy` (`Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree.lean:125`) and every real chart family
160	is built from.
161	
162	Stated because this, not `isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_pointwise`, is what a coverage lane
163	owes when the atlas is restricted: the two differ by exactly `hV`. -/
164	theorem isLocallySurjective_restrictChart_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
165	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) (V : ∀ i, (X i).Opens)
166	    (h : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
167	      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
168	        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s ∧
169	          Set.range (x.base) ⊆ Set.range ((V i).ι.base)) :
170	    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology
171	      (Sigma.desc (fun i => restrictChart (f i) (V i))) :=
172	  isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_pointwise C _ (liftPointwiseToOpens C f V h)
173	
174	/-! ## The converse: `hV` is the exact difference, not a convenient extra
175	
176	A coupling lemma whose hypothesis is stronger than the gap it bridges hides the gap instead of
177	naming it.  This section rules that out: restricted coverage gives back unrestricted coverage
178	together with the containment, so `hV` is precisely what separates the two. -/
179	
180	variable (C) in
181	/-- **The converse of the coupling.**  Pointwise coverage for the restricted family gives
182	pointwise coverage for `f` *and* the range containment at the produced witness.
183	
184	So `liftPointwiseToOpens`' hypothesis is not a strengthening chosen to make the proof go: it
185	is logically equivalent to the conclusion.  In particular a lane cannot obtain B-6 for the
186	restricted atlas — the one the seam consumes — while avoiding the statement that coverage hits
187	its classes inside `V i`.
188	
189	The witness is `x ≫ (V i).ι`, whose range is contained in that of `(V i).ι` by construction,
190	and whose chart value under `f i` is the restricted chart's value at `x` by
191	`restrictChart_app_apply`. -/
192	theorem pointwise_of_pointwise_restrictChart {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
193	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) (V : ∀ i, (X i).Opens)
194	    (h : PointwiseCoverage C (fun i => restrictChart (f i) (V i))) :
195	    ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
196	      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
197	        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s ∧
198	          Set.range (x.base) ⊆ Set.range ((V i).ι.base) := by
199	  intro T s t
200	  obtain ⟨W, htW, i, u, hu⟩ := h T s t
201	  refine ⟨W, htW, i, u ≫ (V i).ι, hu, ?_⟩
202	  intro z hz
203	  obtain ⟨w, rfl⟩ := hz
204	  exact ⟨u.base w, rfl⟩
205	
206	end
207	
208	end AlgebraicGeometry

1	/-
